newsitem.title: UK: UK shares close sharply lower amid rate anxiety.
newsitem.headline: UK shares close sharply lower amid rate anxiety.

text.p: Leading blue chips stumbled on Monday from record levels set last week amid concerns about monetary policy on both sides of the Atlantic, traders said. The FTSE 100 closed 44.4 points lower at 3,919.7, after climbing to a record at 3,994.1 on Friday.
Dividend payouts trimmed 8.17 points from the leading blue chip index. But losses were broadbased, with decliners beating advancers by a margin of nine to one.
It was the biggest one-day drop since July 16, when a Wall Street-inspired selloff knocked off 66 points from the FTSE 100. Volume was light, with only 436.0 million shares recorded.

A trader added, "I still think the market is okay underneath," said the head of trading at one brokerage. "4,000 is very much on the cards. There is not a lot of selling and there is plenty of value out there."
Economists surveyed by Reuters were not expecting a change in UK rates after today's meeting, which lasted almost an hour.
Any change in policy would probably be signalled by the Bank of England via money market operations early on Tuesday.
But analysts and traders were divided about whether the Federal Reserve would tighten.
Some expect U.S. policy makers, due to meet tomorrow afternoon (London time), to up rates as much as 50 basis points. While others look for a 25 basis point increase or no change.
Wall Street was down 36 points when London markets closed.

Shares in UK retailers dropped as the prospect of tighter credit prompted a round of profit-taking in a sector that has been one of the main motors driving the UK equity market this year, traders said.
Marks & Spencer fell 7-1/2p to 501p. Next Plc lost 15-1/2p to 552-1/2p. Dixons Group eased 7-1/2p to 553p, and Great Universal Stores slumped 16p to 621-1/2p.
